purpose: Vivi Storybook is the fast UI regression lab and facade-review surface for the local document viewer. Every product-facing UI slice should be represented by at least one stable story and, when the behavior is interactive, one representative interaction story.

reviewStages.label: HTML Concept Mock
reviewStages.intent: Use docs/ui-mocks to compare layout, density, information hierarchy, and product direction before React implementation.

reviewStages.label: Storybook Facade
reviewStages.intent: Use React components with static props, simplified callbacks, and domain-shaped fixtures as the design approval surface before real application, backend, filesystem, SSE, route, or preview behavior is wired.

reviewStages.label: Wired Feature
reviewStages.intent: After explicit approval, connect the approved facade to real application state, use cases, infrastructure, and server behavior while preserving useful facade stories as visual contracts.

surfaces.label: Design review flow
surfaces.intent: Make Vivi's HTML Concept Mock -> Storybook Facade -> Wired Feature workflow visible inside Storybook itself.
reviewFocus: reviewers can see why a facade story may be static
agents can identify the current GUI review stage
Storybook communicates the distinction between visual approval and wired behavior

surfaces.label: Quiet reader refinement
surfaces.intent: Wire approved Quiet Reader concept A and sidebar H1 concept B into the real workbench, preserving the reviewed facade as a visual contract. Sidebar structure follows mock 49 B: folder-only outline icons and subtle hierarchy guides.
reviewFocus: tab management is available through one keyboard-accessible menu
duplicate, preview, and changed documents retain their identity
empty-state search opens a fixture document
narrow and split layouts preserve the directory map and document context
new workspaces start at 210 / 310 px and saved sizes are preserved
the real empty reader opens the document palette and explains the feedback loop
a labeled compact inspector disclosure keeps Review Queue and Document reachable
folder glyphs and hierarchy guides carry structure; document rows retain filename/H1 without a file icon

surfaces.label: Document-first reader
surfaces.intent: Define the replacement product surface: open a document, read naturally, comment on any block, and reveal changes only as an optional lens.
reviewFocus: normal reading is the default state and does not imply a review queue
every rendered block uses the same hover and double-click comment affordance whether or not it changed
single click and drag remain ordinary text-selection gestures and never open comment input
comment input and feedback stay attached to the document location
change context appears only after the reader enables the Changes lens
the sidebar preserves the real nested directory structure while hiding non-document files and empty directories

surfaces.label: Wired document inspector
surfaces.intent: Connect the approved document-first hierarchy to the active file, outline, feedback, drafts, and optional change evidence used by the real workbench.
reviewFocus: the repository-wide review queue remains the default work surface
Review Queue and Document remain visible as two stable inspector tabs with a clear active state
the current document inspector remains directly reachable from the queue and can return to the preserved review position
outline and feedback navigate the real active document
Changes remains an explicit optional lens
double-click commenting guidance leaves single-click and drag for reading

surfaces.label: Comment attention
surfaces.intent: Represent pending and published human feedback plus the agent seen receipt as a compact attention model.
reviewFocus: draft comments read as private until publish
pending drafts can be deleted before publish
agent reads are visible as Seen while agent-authored messages stay out of the browser
published feedback exposes its read receipt and an explicit Add new feedback action that creates a separate note rather than a response

surfaces.label: Unified publish flow
surfaces.intent: Keep saved private feedback recognizable across Review Queue and Document while making the publish scope explicit.
reviewFocus: Review Queue publishes ready feedback across the workspace
Document publishes only ready feedback from the current document
typing input is recoverable but visibly excluded from Publish
the same component, state labels, action order, and colors survive the inspector tab switch

surfaces.label: Review Queue signal ledger
surfaces.intent: Keep the right inspector compact by presenting one attention-ordered file ledger with signal filters instead of duplicating the Explorer directory tree.
reviewFocus: the left Explorer remains the only directory hierarchy
All, Unseen, Drafts, and Changed filters expose their counts and preserve attention ordering
each row keeps the parent path as secondary metadata for disambiguation
draft publication stays available on the actionable file row
recent activity expires after 30 minutes while drafts and unseen feedback remain pinned
inputs are listed only for open files and every listed input resumes its exact session
missing sources leave active counts and navigation while their feedback remains inspectable in a collapsed unavailable section

surfaces.label: Document viewer coverage
surfaces.intent: Cover the two product document surfaces: rendered/source Markdown and sandboxed/source HTML.
reviewFocus: Markdown and HTML remain readable without implying editing
rendered and source modes preserve document context
Markdown and HTML use one anchored no-reflow rendered-feedback popover
HTML preview remains sandboxed and common Mermaid markup renders as SVG
projected legacy HTML feedback is owned by the viewer without a duplicate global card
passive comments keep markers without persistent block fills; only the open/input target gets a bounded wash
comment markers are excluded from the text-layer positioning rule and Markdown markers occupy the right margin without reflow
one compact native view selector preserves source/rendered state, source-input return, and optional Changes
At intermediate pane widths, the path/current-comment row and viewer controls stack without overlapping the HTML sandbox state.
Relative embedded images resolve under the selected workspace; image-only blocks preserve source anchors and can open published feedback or a new input.

surfaces.label: Resumable comment composer
surfaces.intent: Preserve typed, unpublished feedback across real viewer and navigation transitions while keeping Save and Publish explicit.
reviewFocus: same-file thoughts can remain open together
outside click and Escape never silently discard typed feedback
file and tab navigation preserves local input
saved drafts and local unsent input remain visibly distinct
stale anchors require explicit re-anchor or discard

surfaces.label: Document changes lens
surfaces.intent: Keep Markdown and HTML change evidence available as an optional lens without turning it into the primary workflow.
reviewFocus: normal document reading remains the default
change comments stay anchored to the document surface
rendered Markdown and HTML changes remain readable

surfaces.label: Navigation overlays
surfaces.intent: Cover Cmd/Ctrl+K quick open, text search, command mode, shortcut help, topbar, tree, and tabs.
reviewFocus: overlays feel modal rather than permanent layout
keyboard focus and dismissal behavior are reviewable
search results make the next action obvious
Real file names remain primary; first H1 is secondary and updates without changing paths or order
Connection failures and unpublished drafts stay visible at compact widths; operational detail opens with pointer or keyboard and dismisses with Escape or outside focus.

surfaces.label: Quiet sidebar selection A
surfaces.intent: Wire accepted concept 50 A into TreeSidebar, retaining the facade and checking collapsed ancestry and independent keyboard focus in the integrated SidebarStructure story.
reviewFocus: selection and keyboard focus remain independent
collapsed ancestry preserves the hidden current location
open state does not repeat OPEN labels or occupy a third line

agentWorkflow: Use HTML Concept Mock -> Storybook Facade -> Wired Feature for meaningful GUI changes unless the user explicitly asks to skip it.
Read ui/src/storybook/README.md before changing product UI.
Confirm whether the current work is in the html-concept, storybook-facade, or wired-feature stage.
Update or add a story for every user-visible UI state you changed.
Facade stories may use static props, simplified callbacks, and domain-shaped fixtures; they must not mock filesystem watchers, HTTP routes, GraphQL transport, SSE, or real preview server behavior.
If the UI introduces a new product-facing surface, add it to this manifest.
Add a play interaction for one representative story when the change affects keyboard, pointer, focus, or form behavior.
Run task storybook:verify and task storybook:build before handing off UI changes.
